subject: Commitment window, fallback routing & KV-cache telemetry request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Lindström <sarah@edgecompute.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commitment window, fallback routing & KV-cache telemetry request

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As we prepare a dedicated capacity proposal for EdgeCompute.ai (DEAL-8342-EDGE) I need a couple of focused pieces of telemetry so we can size the reserved fleet and the burst capacity correctly. Keeping it short — could you share the following by EOD Tuesday if possible?

1) Traffic sample CSV (attached): a 7-day snippet with UTC timestamps, endpoint route, request type (chat/generate/embed), prompt token count, response token count, and a session id or user id column if available. We received an initial sample but the one attached in this thread has two additional columns I requested (session_id, is_prefetch).

2) KV-cache telemetry: we need a small JSON sample showing KV cache hit/miss rates by route and median TTL/invalidation window. If you have prefix cache hit ratios vs KV-cache hits, include both.

3) Commitment window: what committed throughput or percent-of-peak are you comfortable locking for 12 months vs wanting a variable burst pool? Example: 60% committed, 40% burst. If you have internal procurement constraints (min committed GPUs, budget cadence), include those.

4) Fallback policy tolerance: how tolerant is the product to model quality regressions when we failover to a lower-footprint variant during spikes? Give an acceptable max delta (e.g., 3–5% QA metric drop or an example of degraded cases you’d accept).

Attachments: edge-traffic-samples.csv, kvcache-telemetry-sample.json (both included with this mail). I’ve also attached a one-page template (dedicated-sizer-template.xlsx) to make answers quick.

Irene and Marissa — I’ve looped you for sizing and cost estimates; Karthik will drive the GPU mix once we have the traffic and KV numbers.

Next step: once we get the two telemetry artifacts and your target commitment window, we’ll run a preliminary sizing run and send a short recommended mix and burst policy for review.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.inference

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment window, fallback routing & KV-cache telemetry request

Hi Naomi —

Thanks — attaching what we have. High level answers inline:

1) Traffic sample: attached CSV contains 7 days from 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-11. Typical mix today is ~70% chat/interactive, 25% generate (batch micro-batches), 5% embeddings. Mean prompt length is ~120 tokens; median response length is 220 tokens but tail at p99 can be 1,200 tokens for long-form summarization. Peak day QPS in that week was 1,200 rps global, but note we have an evening spike in US-Pacific that accounts for ~45% of daily volume.

2) KV-cache telemetry: attached JSON has route-level hit/miss and an aggregated prefix-hit column. Current cold-start miss is ~18% overall; warm runs see ~82% KV hit on stable conversational flows. Typical KV TTL is session-bound (~30–45 minutes) with some longer-lived caches for user profiles (~6h).

3) Commitment: procurement is targeting a 12-month reserved plan but procurement wants a minimum of 12 reserved A100-80GB equiv or the dollar equivalent. Our product org is willing to commit ~50–65% of expected average daily throughput, but wants option to burst for up to 4 consecutive hours at 2x baseline during launches.

4) Fallback tolerance: product requirement is strict on critical flows (billing-related and policy moderation) — we need parity there (no regressions). Non-critical recommendation/assistant flows can tolerate up to a 5% QA drop for short failovers.

Attaching: edge-traffic-samples.csv, kvcache-telemetry-sample.json, and a short draft of our procurement terms (MVP-commitment-terms.pdf).

Let me know if you need raw traces or p99 response-time histograms.

Cheers,
Sarah
Head of Infrastructure, EdgeCompute.ai

Subject: Re: Commitment window, fallback routing & KV-cache telemetry request

Thanks Sarah — this is super helpful. Short clarifying items before Karthik and I run a preliminary sizing:

- Can you export a 1-hour trace for one of your evening spikes (UTC timestamps) including per-request server-side latency (client->model->response), and whether the request used a cached prefix or a cold load? That lets us model queueing/backpressure and the marginal CPU/GPU work per token on cold vs warm paths.

- For KV-cache: do you have a distribution of TTLs (percent of keys with <5m, 5–30m, 30–360m, >360m)? If a large fraction is >6h that changes the memory sizing for per-GPU KV caches.

- Regarding fallback: we’ll propose a staged fallback policy — first route to a quantized variant of the same model (faster, lower memory), then to a smaller-family model if still constrained. To model the impact, we need a short list of the product flows where the 0% regression requirement applies (you mentioned billing and moderation). If you can flag those as route ids in the CSV we’ll pin them as non-degradable.

Marissa — once we have the 1-hour spike and TTL distribution, can you and I run a quick ballpark of per-session KV footprint and the expected cross-session cache hit improvement with a 30% reserved + burst pool vs 50% reserved? I’ll draft the fallback routing policy text for the SOW.

Naomi — recommend we schedule a 45-min deep-dive on Wednesday to walk the team through the traces and our assumptions before sending the formal sizing.

Irene
Product Lead, Dedicated Deployments
Redwood Inference

Weekend read — quick preliminary sizing notes based on the artifacts Sarah sent and Irene's questions. These are ballpark assumptions to align expectations ahead of the deep-dive:

1) Baseline mix & QPS shape used:
- Baseline sustained QPS: 600 rps (global average from the 7-day sample)
- Peak evening spike: ~2.0x baseline for a 3-hour window and 1.5x baseline for an additional 5 hours
- Prompt tokens median 120, response median 220, p99 response up to 1,200 tokens

2) Cache behavior assumptions (from provided JSON):
- KV hit on warm conversational flows: ~82%
- Effective token reduction from hits: ~45% fewer decoded tokens on average for cached requests
- Distribution of TTLs looks roughly: <5m:10%, 5–30m:50%, 30–360m:30%, >360m:10% (will refine with the trace export)

3) Preliminary GPU mix recommendation (reserved + burst):
- Reserved pool (12 mo commit): 12 x A100-80GB (focus on steady-state chat memory + KV RAM). This matches procurement floor and gives headroom for session-level KV caches.
- Burst pool (regional, elastic): 8 x H100 (short-term launches and p99 long responses). Configure burst autoscale to ramp up at sustained queue depth > 75% for > 2 minutes, with max 2x baseline for up to 4 hours as requested.

4) KV-cache sizing note:
- Expect per-GPU KV memory footprint ~90–140 GB across resident keys assuming current TTL mix. With 12 reserved A100-80GB we will shard keys and rely on instance-local cache + ring fallback. If TTL distribution shifts to more >6h keys we will need to increase reserved count or leverage central LRU-backed cache (adds network overhead).

5) Fallback policy suggestion:
- Tier 1: quantized same-architecture variant (approx -30% cost, -5% quality in non-critical flows)
- Tier 2: smaller-family model (2–3x throughput improvement, quality check required)
- Critical routes (billing/moderation): always pin to reserved pool; do not degrade.

6) Next steps & asks:
- Sarah: please provide a 1-hour spike trace and the TTL distribution histogram for keys.
- Naomi: schedule Wed 45-min deep-dive (Irene/Marissa/Karthik + Edge infra + product).
- Marissa/Irene: I’ll share a quick cost delta table for the two fleet mixes above by EOD Wednesday after the deep-dive.

If the above looks directionally correct I’ll convert it into a concise sizing appendix for the SOW and a recommended commitment percentage (I’m leaning toward a 55% reserved / 45% burst split based on their procurement ask and tail risk).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Pre-Sales Capacity Engineering
Redwood Inference
